title: Work IQ: invoke custom agents and agents that call third-party tools
summary: The roadmap facts and the documented control paths are supported. The billing discussion needs a narrower qualification: Microsoft already documents metered Work IQ API use, including actions and tools invoked through Work IQ; what remains unconfirmed is this capability's specific charging treatment, not whether Work IQ API use is metered.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to enable Work IQ to invoke custom agents and agents that call supported third-party tools.
claims.quote: Enable Work IQ to invoke custom agents and agents that call supported third-party tools.

claims.claim: Work IQ API use follows a consumption model using Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether invoking custom agents or third-party-tool agents is metered.
claims.quote: Work IQ API consumption consists of two parts: variable charge for query-style consumption (grounding, retrieval, and reasoning) and a static usage component for actions and tools invoked through Work IQ.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'That page does not mention this roadmap item' with: 'Work IQ API use is metered through Copilot Credits; Microsoft documents variable query-style consumption and a static component for actions and tools invoked through Work IQ. Microsoft has not mapped this roadmap extension to a specific charge or stated whether invoking another agent adds a separate charge.' Cite https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/licensing/news/work-iq-general-availability. In the cost rationale, replace 'whether or at what rate invoking custom or third-party-tool agents is metered' with 'the specific charging treatment for invoking custom or third-party-tool agents'.

In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP.
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.
